_about: Desk Buddy screen design: two round 240x240 GC9A01 screens (left, right) driven by an ESP32-S3 with Arduino_GFX, colours in RGB565. Coordinates are pixels from the top-left of each screen; only the circle centred on (120,120) with radius 120 is visible. Angles are degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock. Elements draw in order (later ones on top). Text "y" is the top of the text (its middle or bottom when "valign" says so; "align" lines each line up on x); "font" is "classic" (the built-in 5x7 font: size n = 6n x 8n px per character, line height 10n px) or an Adafruit-format GFX font such as FreeSans12pt7b (drawn with setFont, baseline at y + ascent, line height = yAdvance; size multiplies it); {placeholders} in text are live data (see "fields"; "customFields" are ones the designer made up, with "source" saying where the value should come from). Ring and hand "value" says what they follow ("field:<key>" = one of the custom fields). "when" says when a scene should be shown, and "alsoWhen" (up to 3 more) adds situations that must be happening at the same time; when several scenes fit, the one needing the most situations wins. "claude_open" is happening whenever Claude has any status, and an exact status scene beats it. While media is paused, "media" and "media_claude" scenes also count (one point below a "paused" scene). "clock12" makes {time} a 12-hour clock ("2:32", with {ampm} = "PM") and {notif_time} "6:42 PM"; false is 24-hour. A scene with "hours" {from, to} (24 h, may run overnight) only shows between those times and wins over an all-day scene for the same "when". An eye's "lidRest" is how far its eyelids rest closed (0-90 %); blinks close fully from there. "colorFrom": "fixed" uses "color"; "app" / "status" follow the app playing (its colour in "apps") or Claude's status; "level" (a ring, bar or hand's own value) and "level:<value>" use the design's usage colours ("levelColors": low, medium, high, max), switching at the percentages in "levelSteps". A screen's "backgroundFrom" can likewise be "status" or "app". An "applogo" shows the logo of the app playing ("app": "auto", e.g. the YouTube logo for YouTube and Chrome's for any other site in Chrome) or of one app; "apps" lists the names the PC helper sends in {app}. A "bar" fills like a ring along "dir" from its "value" ("segments" > 0 = that many blocks "gap" px apart). A "pill" is a badge: one line of text on a rounded box sized to fit it (plus "padX" / "padY"), centred on x with its top at y. An "icon" is drawn from filled shapes, "size" px wide and centred on x, y. A "visualizer" is bars that bounce from the clock (millis()) while media plays and sit low when paused; it is an animation, not real audio. Font "app" ("App style") follows the app playing: Spotify gets a Montserrat ExtraBold lookalike of its typeface, YouTube, YouTube Music and Chrome get Roboto, anything else a bold sans. A "notification" scene shows for a few seconds when a phone notification arrives through Phone Link ({notif_app}, {notif_title}, {notif_text}, {notif_count}: "x37" when it came in 37 times or empty, {notif_time}: "HH:MM"); "colorFrom": "notif" and an applogo with "app": "notif" follow the phone app that sent it. Open the file in the Desk Buddy Screen Designer, or give it to Claude to turn into Arduino code.
